note: Authored by reading Tafsir al-Tabari in English against the reader's modern translation. Each phrase carries the app's own words for that piece of the verse, a plain modern English line of my own, the Arabic of the piece, and the numbered paragraphs of the commentary that speak of it.

phrases.translation: Read, ˹O Prophet,˺ in the Name of your Lord
phrases.text: The command is addressed to Muhammad: recite, in the name of your Lord, with His name mentioned.

phrases.translation: Who created—
phrases.text: Recite with the mention of your Lord who created.

phrases.translation: created humans from a clinging clot
phrases.text: He made man from a clot of blood. Tabari explains that the word means a single clot, though it is written as a plural, because the word for man itself stands in the singular while carrying the sense of a plural.

phrases.translation: Read! And your Lord is the Most Generous
phrases.text: Read again, O Muhammad. Your Lord is the Most Generous, the one who taught by the pen.

phrases.translation: Who taught by the pen—
phrases.text: He taught writing and script. Qatada calls the pen a tremendous favour, for without it the world would not hold together. And this, the commentators say, is the first surah of the Quran sent down to the Prophet.

phrases.translation: taught humanity what they knew not
phrases.text: He taught man writing with the pen when man did not know it, and other things besides that which he did not know.

phrases.translation: Most certainly, one exceeds all bounds
phrases.text: No, this does not become man: that his Lord should form him well, teach him what he did not know, favour him beyond compare, and then he should be ungrateful and raise himself against his Lord.

phrases.translation: once they think they are self-sufficient
phrases.text: He grows arrogant and turns ungrateful toward his Lord, because he thinks he needs nothing. Tabari goes back over the whole passage here, showing how the revelation began and gathering the reports that this was the first surah sent down.

phrases.translation: ˹But˺ surely to your Lord is the return ˹of all˺
phrases.text: To your Lord, O Muhammad, is the return, and then he will taste of a punishment he cannot bear.

phrases.translation: Have you seen the man who prevents
phrases.text: The commentators say this was revealed about Abu Jahl, who said he would set his foot on the Prophet's neck. God asks His Prophet to marvel at the man's ignorance while he forbids the prayer and turns away from the truth.

phrases.translation: a servant ˹of Ours˺ from praying
phrases.text: A servant of Ours, when he prays. Ibn Abbas says that had the man gone on, the wardens of the punishment would have seized him there and then.

phrases.translation: What if this ˹servant˺ is ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.text: Have you seen, if the servant is upon the guidance, that is, upon righteousness and correctness in his prayer to his Lord.

phrases.translation: or encourages righteousness
phrases.text: Or that the man who forbids the prayer should be the one enjoining the fear of God. Qatada says the Prophet was upon the guidance and enjoined godfearingness.

phrases.translation: What if that ˹man˺ persists in denial and turns away
phrases.text: Have you seen if he denies and turns away, that is, if the man refuses the truth and does not hold it to be true.

phrases.translation: Does he not know that Allah sees ˹all˺
phrases.text: Does he not know that God sees him, so that he should fear His power and His punishment? The question is put three times, each time with a different turn.

phrases.translation: But no! If he does not desist, We will certainly drag him by the forelock—
phrases.text: He is not able to tread on the Prophet's neck. If he does not desist, We will take him by the front of his head and subdue and humiliate him, dragging him to the Fire.
phrases.ar: كـَلَّا لَئِن لَّمۡ يَنتَهِ لَنَسۡفَعَۢا بِٱلنَّاصِيَةِ

phrases.translation: a lying, sinful forelock
phrases.text: The forelock is described as lying and sinful, though the description really belongs to the man himself.

phrases.translation: So let him call his associates
phrases.text: Let him call the people of his council hall and his helpers from his clan and his people. When the Prophet rebuffed him, he boasted that he had the largest council of anyone in the valley.

phrases.translation: We will call the wardens of Hell
phrases.text: These are the angels, and the Prophet said that they would have seized the man before the eyes of all.

phrases.translation: Again, no! Never obey him ˹O Prophet˺!
phrases.text: Do not obey him in what he commands you, that is, in leaving the prayer to your Lord.

phrases.translation: Rather, ˹continue to˺ prostrate and draw near ˹to Allah˺
phrases.text: Prostrate before your Lord and draw near to Him by making yourself beloved to Him through obedience, for the man will not be able to harm you and We protect you from him.
